newsitem.title: RUSSIA: World Bank sees big rise in loans to Russia.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees big rise in loans to Russia.

text.p: The World Bank expects its loans to Russia to increase by $2-3 billion a year for the next few years from the current $6 billion, a senior bank official said on Wednesday.
"We would expect that if everything goes well, we can commit additional loans of the order of $2-3 billion a year," said Johannes Linn, vice-president, Europe and Central Asia.
"In principle, a doubling of loans outstanding by the end of the century is not impossible," he told a news conference.

The World Bank has so far committed $6.2 billion to Russia, of which $2.7 billion has been disbursed, he said. Disbursements are running at a monthly rate of $70 million, up from $25 million a year ago.

World Bank Moscow representative Michael Carter said the next loans in the works would fund a bureau for economic analysis to improve economic policy-making and higher education and school textbooks, and that work on a Structural Adjustment Loan would be completed in the next few months.
